description:
## Goal

src/infrastructure/actor.cr allocates a fresh
Channel(String).new(1) for every def_call (lines ~245 and ~300).
A def_call also allocates a Call{Method} struct and a JSON
reply string. On 30s timeout the channel + struct linger for
30s; on caller-raises-after-send they linger until GC.

Under a busy server (hundreds of API requests / min) this
allocates and frees thousands of channels / hour. The Crystal GC
handles this fine in steady state, but the JSON-string boxing
and struct churn add overhead and obscure the true heap
residents.

## Approach

1. Pool reply channels per-fiber using a thread-local stack
   (FIFO push/pop). Each fiber maintains up to N idle channels
   and reuses them across def_call invocations. This eliminates
   ~all channel allocations on the hot path.
2. On timeout, the channel is returned to the pool with its
   buffer cleared.
3. The macro-generated Call{Method} structs are still
   allocated per call — those are small and the polymorphic
   dispatch requires it. Focus on the channel allocation only.
4. Add a counter for "reply channels allocated" vs "reply
   channels reused" so we can verify the optimization in the
   memory log (cf. task 1).

## Acceptance

- Reply channel allocations per minute drops by >90% on a
  representative API workload (verify with the new counter).
- No behavior change visible to callers; existing spec suite
  passes unchanged.
- Build + ameba clean.
title: Reduce per-def_call Channel allocations in Actor framework
